verdict.rationale: The Models page documents concrete limits of 250,000 tokens per second and 1,200 requests per minute. It says a request over either limit returns 429 Too Many Requests, that SDKs retry with backoff and honor retry-after, and the JS SDK has a dedicated RateLimitError class for HTTP 429. Tier scaling gets only a brief mention that enterprise plans offer higher limits, and the docs warn the limits can change without notice. missing for 10: a per-tier rate-limit table showing how limits scale, documented 429 response body/headers beyond retry-after, independent corroboration of the limits.

support.subject: As a developer, I can read documented rate limits — requests and tokens per unit time, how tiers scale, and what a 429 looks like — before I hit them in production

citations.quote: 250,000 tokens per second / 1,200 requests per minute
A request over either limit returns `429 Too Many Requests`. Our client SDKs retry with backoff by default and honor the `retry-after` header
HTTP 429: the rate limit was exceeded.
Configure retries with RetryPolicy — attempt count, retryable statuses, backoff, and retry headers handling.
